name: ore-haul-dispatch
description: Regression scenario for #671: collectedOre.<material> never rose via automatic haul dispatch because estimateActionCost/selectBestActionForEmployee (ActionSelection.ts) ranked haul_debris/fragment_debris candidates purely by travel-time cost, with zero ore-awareness. A small Tier 1 freight_warehouse (2000kg, BuildingDefs.ts) fills solid from the first cheapest (nearest, ore-agnostic) fragments and permanently excludes remaining ones -- including ore-bearing ones, since nothing frees warehouse room except a player's own contract sale. Seed 10's 3x3 drill grid at (18,19) deterministically exposes ~250 ore-bearing ground fragments alongside plenty of plain rock (sandbox-confirmed end to end against the real, un-cheated console pipeline -- no fixture injection, no forced needs gauges, exact ids/commands below reproduced verbatim): under today's pure-travel-time ranking, the warehouse fills solid from plain spoil alone (stuck permanently at storedMassKg 2125/2000, confirmed unchanged 500+ ticks past the build) and collectedOreTotal never rises off zero. Once ActionSelection.ts's estimateActionCost subtracts ORE_HAUL_PRIORITY_BONUS_TICKS for ore-bearing candidates (haulActionCarriesOre, HaulDispatch.ts), an ore fragment should outrank at least some nearby plain ones and get delivered before the warehouse fills solid. Runs correctly in both command mode and interaction mode: every state-dependent step below carries a real, click-driven interaction array, so interaction mode drives the same mutations through the UI rather than falling back to the console.

steps.command: new_game mine_type:desert seed:10 size:64 staffed:true cash:200000

interaction.command: new_game mine_type:desert seed:10 size:64 staffed:true cash:200000

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:3 cols:3 spacing:3 depth:8 start:18,19 diameter:0.089
steps.description: 9-hole grid, deterministic under seed 10 -- sandbox-confirmed to expose ~250 ore-bearing ground fragments alongside plenty of plain rock once blasted. diameter:0.089 added to match the real grid-tool confirm's own DEFAULT_DIAMETER_M (Drill.ts) -- an omitted diameter fell back to a different console-only default (0.15, mining.ts), desyncing drill duration/tick timing against interaction mode (same fix as rock-fragmenter-breaking.json's own drill_plan step).
#553: drain the ordered plan -- the staffed driller/drill_rig lands all 9 holes well inside this budget (sandbox-measured landing at tick 166 under real, un-cheated needs gauges).
DEFAULT_AMOUNT_KG (5) and DEFAULT_STEMMING_M (2) in Charge.ts already match this command's declared amount/stemming, so no stepper clicks are needed before Charge All.
#554: drain the charge order(s) queued by the step above (charging is real work, not instant) before continuing.

expect.note: a fired blast clears the plan back to zero -- nothing has been hauled anywhere yet, so collectedOreTotal is still 0 at this point

steps.description: #553: staffed:true's roster (driller/blaster/driver/driver/driver, ids 1-5 -- STARTING_SITE_STAFFED_COMPOSITION, balance.ts) means this hire is the roster's 6th employee, not its 1st. It also means employees 3-5 already hold driving licences (one driving.truck, two driving.excavator) and vehicle #2 is already a debris_hauler -- this scenario deliberately hires/buys a fresh driver+hauler and addresses both by their explicit new ids (6/5) below rather than "the first driver"/"the first debris_hauler", which would instead resolve to one of the pre-existing staffed ones.

Left unmarked: hiring already grants the Rookie driving.truck qualification (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION in Employee.ts); this only raises the level for the scenario's needs -- the player-facing path is `employee train`. Bootstrap-only primitive (BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_ALLOWLIST), no UI equivalent by design.

#553: staffed:true's fleet (drill_rig/debris_hauler/rock_digger/rock_fragmenter, ids 1-4) means this purchase is the fleet's 5th vehicle, not its 1st -- and the blast above destroyed the drill_rig (vehicle #1, sitting inside its own hole's blast radius), so vehicleCount goes 3 -> 4, not 0 -> 1.

Vehicle 5 (the debris_hauler just bought) and employee 6 (the driver just hired) -- staffed:true's fleet/roster occupy ids 1-4/1-5. #921: Fleet panel's Assign/Unassign controls removed; vehicles are now claimed automatically by a qualified employee when a vehicle-gated task needs one, so this step runs as a direct bootstrap primitive instead of a click.
Default Tier 1 freight_warehouse capacity (BuildingDefs.ts) -- small relative to the blast's total haulable mass, which is the whole point of this scenario.
Let the queued construction site(s) be walked to and built out (#556): ordering a building no longer places it, so everything below that needs a standing building waits here first.

The real wait for automatic haul dispatch to run its course, expressed as a tickCount target (rather than a plain `tick 200`) so waitUntil's own internal event-auto-resolution (issue #590) carries this step through any spontaneous event instead of a bare `tick` refusing outright the instant one fires mid-window -- sandbox-confirmed against this exact seed/setup: tickCount reads 228 immediately before this step, so 428 is 200 real ticks of dispatch beyond that, with max_ticks:260 leaving slack for a handful of event-resolution iterations along the way. Sandbox-confirmed on today's (buggy) code: the warehouse is already permanently full (storedMassKg 2125/2000, unchanged 300+ ticks past this window) by the time this step ends, with collectedOreTotal stuck at 0 the whole way. This is the fix's own acceptance check: collectedOreTotal must rise off zero once ore-bearing candidates can jump the queue ahead of plain spoil while the warehouse still has room.

expect.note: collectedOreTotal is this fix's own acceptance check (#671). storedMassKg is the regression check alongside it -- the new ore-priority ranking must not starve out generic spoil delivery entirely; some non-ore mass should still make it into storage alongside the ore.
